name: sol_integrations_layerzero_7
description: Insufficient LayerZero block confirmations enabling reorg-based message forgery
question: The source file in `source` configures a LayerZero endpoint, relayer, or oracle by setting the required block confirmations parameter to 0 or to a hardcoded trivial value (e.g. 1) without any chain-specific justification, allowing cross-chain messages to be relayed or accepted before the source chain block has reached finality, so a chain reorg could let an attacker forge, duplicate, or reverse a relayed message.
criteria: setConfig or a LayerZero UlnConfig struct sets confirmations to 0 for a chain, meaning messages can be relayed without waiting for any block finality
A constant or default value like CONFIRMATIONS = 1 is hardcoded and applied uniformly to all destination chains regardless of their known reorg depth
The contract deploys or initializes a LayerZero endpoint/relay configuration where the confirmations field is left unset (defaulting to zero) before enabling message sending
